title: The digest gets wet
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The rack by the laundromat door: the storm blew in. The week's digests are pulp. The owner dries one in a dryer. It comes out a ball. She keeps the ball.

panels.composition: The laundromat. The door blown open, rain on the floor, the rack tipped, digests soaked. The LAUNDRY owner with a mop. WOOD arriving.

image.prompt: a laundromat with its front door blown open and a tipped wire rack of soaked booklets on the wet floor, the owner with a mop, black and white, no words

panels.composition: One digest going into a dryer with a towel.

image.prompt: close on a hand putting a soaked booklet and a towel into a laundromat dryer, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dryer's window. The digest going round. Wood and the owner watching it go.

image.prompt: a young man and a laundromat owner watching a dryer's round window as something small tumbles inside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dryer open. The digest: a warm gray ball the size of a fist. The owner setting it on the counter. Keeping it.

image.prompt: close on a laundromat counter with a small gray ball of dried paper pulp set on it beside a cash register, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first ball. She keeps it on the counter for years.
